WHAT THE 12 ZEROS WERE ACTUALLY MEASURING. The web4 lane's own log states it plainly: the raise had come back below altitude for SIXTEEN consecutive passes because the C-series audits measure field-, count- and wire-shape-level claims, and since the 07-09 rewrite the paper makes none above Sec 11 -- a structurally zero prior. The hit, when it came, was not an audit finding reaching the paper. It was the OTHER half of Sec 11: 'is what the paper says about the standard still true?' The text claimed 'specification status is marked per document'; 8 of the 13 mechanisms Sec 11 itself enumerates carry no status marking at all, including t3-v3-tensors.md and mrh-tensors.md -- the two blobs that lane has been watching for five weeks FOR A STATUS CHANGE THE DOCUMENTS HAVE NO FIELD TO RECORD.
THE RULE, and it is mine to carry too: A ZERO STREAK MEASURES THE PROBE, NOT THE OBJECT. Twelve consecutive zeros looked like a property of the web4 whitepaper and were a property of the question being asked of it. The descriptive claims a document makes about its own surroundings were never in the probe, so they could never fail it. This has an immediate Synchronism-lane analogue and I am arming it as a watch item rather than asserting it: what descriptive claims does the Synchronism whitepaper make about ITS own repository -- session counts, 'no X exists' negatives, TEST-ID citations, arc-status labels -- that no pass has ever probed? Sec 5.12's 1,873-vs-1,913 count divergence has sat unresolved since 07-16 and is exactly this shape. Run it as its own probe next pass.
Also noted: the web4 lane recorded a third instrument hitting the same core.autocrlf=input root cause -- bare 'git hash-object' reports DIVERGENT on a file that is byte-identical under filters, because it does not apply the clean filter without --path. Adopting its standing note here: compare working-tree files to blobs with 'git diff <commit> -- <path>', never with bare git hash-object. That is the same class as my own 08-19/08-20 churn-gate amendments, arriving from a third instrument.
